# David Blazar

<div class="hero-title">Associate Professor of Education Policy<br>College of Education, University of Maryland, College Park</div>

<a class="btn-accent" href="mailto:dblazar@umd.edu">Email</a>&nbsp;
<a class="btn-outline" href="files/David-Blazar-CV.pdf">Download CV</a>&nbsp;
<a class="btn-outline" href="https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=atIXv0UAAAAJ&hl=en">Google Scholar</a>
:::
:::

David Blazar is an Associate Professor of Education Policy in the College of Education at the University of Maryland, College Park, where he also directs the [Maryland Equity Project](https://education.umd.edu/research/centers/mep), serves as principal investigator for the research branch of the [Maryland Longitudinal Data System](https://mldscenter.maryland.gov/), and holds an affiliate appointment in the School of Public Policy. His research examines the effective, efficient, and equitable allocation of resources in schools — particularly resources related to teachers — spanning three broad areas: the characteristics of effective teachers and teaching practices; whether and how instructional resources such as coaching, curricula, and evaluation systems improve teacher practice and student outcomes; and the labor market policies and practices that shape who becomes, and remains, a teacher.

Before entering academia, David taught high school English Language Arts in New York City. He holds a doctorate in Quantitative Policy Analysis in Education and a master's degree in Education Policy and Management, both from the Harvard Graduate School of Education.
